thread.title: Asian markets roll along on Powell’s comments; Nikkei up for 5th straight day - MarketWatch

author: Dow Jones Newswires
title: Asian markets roll along on Powell’s comments; Nikkei up for 5th straight day - MarketWatch
text:
Asian stock markets logged solid gains Thursday after the 2%-plus jumps got major averages in the U.S. after Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell’s comments hinted at a slower pace of Fed interest-rate increases next year.
Read: Did Fed’s Powell ‘light the fuse’ for a year-end stock-market rally?
Japanese stocks were up for the fifth straight session, with the Nikkei NIK, +0.39% 0.4% higher. Among individual stocks, Nintendo 7974, +4.06% was up more than 4% and SoftBank 9984, +3.06% gained more than 3%. Still, some risk persists. With the dollar USDJPY, -0.37% sitting around ¥113.42 during Asian trading compared with ¥113.68 in late New York trade, the 20-year Japanese government bond’s yield was lower at 0.605%.
Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index HSI, -0.87% gave up early gains to close down 0.8%. Index heavyweight Tencent 0700, -0.89% fell nearly 1% while property developer Sun Hung Kai Properties 2949, -1.47% fell 1.5%.
China’s benchmarks were slightly higher initially, with investors are on their toes for the weekend meeting between presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. The Shanghai Composite SHCOMP, -1.32% and the Shenzhen Composite 399106, -2.21% swung between slight gains and losses before a lower finish for both. Nomura analysts remain wary of the trade summit, calling the meeting “a high-stakes dinner but the menu might not include a trade deal.”
South Korea’s Kospi SEU, +0.28% rose 0.2% as Samsung 005930, +0.00% gained slightly. Taiwan’s Taiex Y9999, +0.01% gained 0.01% as Apple Inc. AAPL, +3.85% suppliers Largan Precision 3008, +1.15% and Taiwan Semiconductor 2330, +1.10% advanced. Singapore’s benchmark index STI, +0.48% was up slightly, ending off higher early levels.
Down Under, Australia’s ASX 200 XJO, +0.58% improved 0.6%, with Rio Tinto RIO, +1.74% and BHP Billiton BHP, +1.21% each up more than 1%. New Zealand’s benchmark NZ50GR, +0.93% rose about 1%.
